titleEn: The Tibetan Book of the Dead — The last Īśvarīs and the gatekeepers; all as one's own appearance; Yama, Lord of Death, and the call on the yidam
part: 12 · The last Īśvarīs and the gatekeepers; all as one's own appearance; Yama, Lord of Death, and the call on the yidam
draftNote: Read from one blockprint at the resolution of an online scan; doubtful places are marked in the notes, and the text has not yet been collated with other prints.
source: Zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol las: Khro bo'i bar do 'char tshul bstan pa (the wrathful deities), pages 107–115 of the reproduction, from an undated Tibetan blockprint of the Thos grol cycle reproduced by the Buddhist Digital Resource Center as W23710 (text ga), read from the page images. It is a traditional blockprint, so no modern editor's work is involved. Two transcriptions found online, one of this print and one of another, were used to check the reading and are not the text. The page gives the print's wording and spelling. Three things are ours: the spaces between words, which Tibetan does not write; the line-end abbreviations, written out; and clear misprints corrected, each named in its note. Where another print reads differently in a way that matters, the note says so. Letters: the Wylie system (Extended Wylie for the Sanskrit words). Pronunciation: the reading style of central Tibet in the THL Simplified Phonetic Transcription (Germano and Tournadre, 2003), produced by rule from the spelling; a living reader's pronunciation will differ in places. The translation is new, made from the Tibetan. Still to do: the text has been read from one print at the resolution of an online scan, and doubtful places are marked in the notes; it has not been collated with the other blockprints.

sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! South from, Delight yellow, pha-wad(?) head, hand in razor holding, and; Peaceful-One red, sea-monster head, hand in vase holding, and;
sentences.i: O child of noble family, from the south: the yellow Delight, with the head of a bat(?), holding a razor in her hand; the red Peaceful One, makara-headed, holding a vase;
sentences.n: The six Īśvarīs of the south, after the six of the east at the end of 011. As there, each is named and given her colour, her animal's head and what she holds; the names are translated. dga' ba, 'delight' (dga', 'glad'); the other recension calls this goddess rdo rje, 'Vajra'. pha wad: the first letter is doubtful ([?]): its tick may be a tsheg fused to the letter, which would give pa. No word pha wad is known. It is kept as printed and read, with low confidence, as perhaps for pha wang, 'bat', one letter off; the other recension has phag mgo ma, 'sow-headed'. spu gri, 'razor'. zhi ba, 'peaceful', here a goddess's name. chu srin, 'water monster', the makara, as in 011. bum pa, 'vase'. kyai is printed with two e-signs, as in 011.

sentences.l: Gods'(?) yogins six own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawning come. Them at not fear!
sentences.i: These six divine(?) yoginīs come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you. Do not fear them.
sentences.n: The sentence that closed the east in 011. lha'i, 'of the gods, divine', stands where the other quarters have their own name (shar gyi in 011, nub kyi and byang gi below); one would expect lho'i, 'of the south', but the other recension also has lha'i, and the print is followed. rnal 'byor, 'yogin', here without the feminine -ma that the other quarters have and the other recension has. The print adds rang gi, 'your own', before klad pa'i, as for the east.

sentences.n: de ltar ngo ma shes na, 'if (you) do not recognise (them) so': ma ... na. khyed, 'you', the polite or plural form, where the text mostly has khyod. zhed cing bred pas, 'fearing and dreading, because' (zhed, 'to fear'; bred, 'to be scared'): bred is doubtful on the image ([?]), though it fits the traces and the other recension has it. slar, 'again, back'. sdug bsngal gyi snon mar 'gro go is obscure, and its sense is uncertain. snon is 'to add', and snon ma could be 'an addition', which gives 'go to an addition of suffering', 'go on to more suffering'. sentences.n: As printed, the sentence says 'if you recognise (them) as your own appearance': there is no negative. sentences.l: 'Me, the between's narrow-pass in, meeting for coming is. For-refuge I-go': thinking's devotion longingly please-make!
sentences.i: With all your longing, have the devotion that thinks: 'He is coming to meet me in the narrow pass of the bardo; I go to him for refuge.'
sentences.n: bdag, 'I, me', the humble word: the dead person speaks. bar do'i 'phrang, 'the narrow pass of the bardo' ('phrang, 'defile, a dangerous narrow way'). bsu ba la, 'to meet, to welcome'. 'byon par 'dug go, 'is coming' ('byon, the respectful verb 'to come, to go'; 'dug after -par, 'is in the act of'), with the sentence-ending -o. skyabs su mchi'o, 'I go for refuge' (mchi, the humble 'go'). snyam pa'i, 'thinking', closes the words of the thought, as in the earlier parts. mos pa, 'devotion'; dung dung, 'intensely, with longing'; mdzod cig, 'please do!', the respectful command.

sentences.l: Jewels-three after-ly remembering do! You-yourself's yidam whatever is, that, remembering do!
sentences.i: Call the Three Jewels to mind. Remember your own yidam, whoever he is.
sentences.n: dkon mchog gsum, 'the Three Jewels', the Buddha, the teaching and the community (dkon mchog, 'rare and supreme'). rjes su dran pa, 'to recollect, to call to mind' (rjes su, 'after, following'; dran pa, 'to remember'). gang yin pa de, 'whatever that is'. The other recension has yi dam gyi lha, 'yidam deity'; the print has yi dam alone.

sentences.l: Name by, whatever emerges(?), call! 'I, the between-in wandered am-because, help to run! Compassion-by hold! Yidam precious!' so called, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Call him by name, whatever name comes to you(?): 'I am wandering in the bardo: run to help me! Hold me with your compassion, precious yidam!' Call out so, and pray.
sentences.n: mtshan, 'name', the respectful word; mtshan nas bos, 'call by name', as ming nas bos in the formula of the days before. gang thon is uncertain: thon is doubtful on the image ([?]), and gang thon is read 'whatever comes out', whatever name comes to mind (thon, 'to come out'); the other recension has only mtshan nas bos shig. bos cig: bos, the past and imperative stem of 'bod, 'to call' ('bod / bos / bod / bos), as in 006, with cig where shig is usual after -s. bar dor 'khyams nas yod pas, 'because (I) am wandering in the bardo' ('khyams nas yod, 'having wandered, am'). ra mda', 'help, rescue'; ra mda' la rgyug cig, 'run to help!' (rgyug, 'to run'), where the other recension has ra mda' mdzod cig, 'give help!'. thugs rjes bzung zhig, 'hold (me) with compassion!' (bzung, the past stem of 'dzin, 'to hold', where the imperative is zung; zhig marks a command after -ng); the other recension has zungs shig, as in 008. rin po che, 'precious'. zhes, 'so', closes the words called. gsol ba thob cig is read, as in the parts before, as a guess for 'pray'. The part ends here; the next begins on the same line, with the call on the lama.

glossary.ཀྱིས: kyis — by, by means of (the 'of' particle + -s; the form used after d, b, s) · after a verb: 'but, and', running on to what follows (yod kyis 'there is, but') · in this print also written where kyi 'of' is meant (sangs rgyas kyis sku, read 'the buddha's bodies')
glossary.ཀྱཻ: kyai — O! a call for attention (also written kye)
glossary.ཀླད་པའི: klad pa'i — of the brain (klad pa 'brain' + -'i 'of')

glossary.ཁམས: khams — realm, world, element (khams): 'jig rten gyi khams 'the realms of the world'
glossary.ཁེངས: khengs — filled, full (khengs, 'to be full'): khengs nas 'having filled'
glossary.ཁོག་ཆེན: khog chen — great trunk (khog 'trunk of the body, hollow' + chen 'great'); perhaps a great carcass, a body without limbs; the sense is not sure (uncertain)
glossary.ཁྭ་ཏའི: khwa ta'i — of the crow (khwa ta 'crow' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཁྱུང: khyung — garuḍa, the great mythical bird (khyung)
glossary.ཁྱེད: khyed — you (khyed), the politer word, also used for more than one: khyed rnams 'you all'
glossary.ཁྲག་འཐུང: khrag 'thung — blood-drinker, blood-drinking: the name of the wrathful deities (khrag 'blood' + 'thung, the present stem of 'to drink', past btungs, imperative 'thungs; Sanskrit heruka)
glossary.ཁྲམ་ཤིང: khram shing — tally-stick, a notched stick for scoring deeds (khram 'tally' + shing 'wood')
glossary.ཁྲོ་བའི: khro ba'i — of wrath, wrathful (khro ba 'wrath, to be wrathful' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཁྲོ་བོ: khro bo — wrathful one, fierce deity (khro 'wrath' + -bo, masculine)
glossary.ཁྲོ་བོའི: khro bo'i — of the wrathful ones, wrathful (khro bo 'wrathful one' + -'i 'of')
glossary.གཅིག: gcig — one; a, a certain · perhaps 'together, at once' (as gcig 'one' in 'od drug kyang gcig 'char du 'ong 'the six lights also dawn together'); the sense is not sure
glossary.གཅོད་པ: gcod pa — cutting (gcod, the present stem of 'to cut' (past bcad), + -pa)
glossary.གཉིས་སུ: gnyis su — into two, as two (gnyis 'two' + -su): gnyis su med par 'without being two, non-dually'
glossary.གནད: gnad — vital point, key point (gnad): the place where a thing is decided, like a pressure point on the body
glossary.གཟུགས: gzugs — form, the body and all that can be seen (gzugs): the first of the five aggregates
glossary.གཤིན་རྗེ: gshin rje — Lord of the Dead, Yama (gshin rje); also the fierce figures of his court
glossary.གཤིན་རྗེ་རུ: gshin rje ru — as Lords of Death (gshin rje 'Lord of the Dead, Yama' + -ru 'as')
glossary.གཤིན་རྗེའི: gshin rje'i — of the Lord of Death, Yama (gshin rje 'lord of the dead' + -'i 'of')
glossary.གསལ་བའི: gsal ba'i — making clear, of clarity (gsal ba 'clear, to be clear' + -'i 'of')

glossary.གི: gi — of (the form used after g, ng); in this print also written where gis 'by' is meant · after a verb: 'and', running on to what follows ('ong gi 'comes, and')

glossary.གྲོལ: grol — to be freed, to come free
glossary.གླགས: glags — opportunity, chance (glags): bzod glags med pa 'with no chance to bear it', unbearable
glossary.གླང: glang — ox, bull (glang); glang chen 'great ox' is the elephant
glossary.ངོ: ngo — face; the nature or identity of a thing
glossary.ཅིང: cing — and, while (links two verbs; also shing, zhing)
glossary.ཆ: cha — part, share, proportion (cha): yab kyi cha 'the father's part' · aspect, side: stong pa'i cha las 'from the empty aspect'

glossary.དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ: dkon mchog gsum — the Three Jewels: the Buddha, the teaching and the community (dkon 'rare' + mchog 'supreme' + gsum 'three')

glossary.དེ་ལྟ་བུའི: de lta bu'i — of that kind, such (de lta bu 'like that' + -'i 'of')
glossary.དེ་ལྟར: de ltar — thus, in that way (de 'that' + ltar 'like')

glossary.དོན་སྙིང: don snying — organs and heart (don 'a solid organ of the body' + snying 'heart')
glossary.དྲག་པོའི: drag po'i — of the fierce, of the strong (drag po 'fierce' + -'i 'of')

glossary.ཕྱི་རོལ་དུ: phyi rol du — outside, in the outer world (phyi rol 'outside' + -du 'in')
glossary.ཕྲལ་བ: phral ba — tearing apart, separating (phral, past stem of 'phral 'to separate, tear apart', + -ba)

about: The fourth part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities, still on the twelfth day. The list of the twenty-eight Īśvarīs goes on: the six of the south, of the west and of the north, each with her colour, her animal's head and what she holds, and then the four gatekeeper yoginīs with the heads of cuckoo, goat, lion and snake, all coming out from inside the dead person's own brain. All of them, the text says, have dawned of themselves from the energy of the self-arisen body: the peaceful deities dawn from the empty aspect of the body of truth, the wrathful from its clear aspect, and to know the fifty-eight blood-drinkers as the natural radiance of one's own awareness is to become a buddha at once. One who does not recognise them sees them as Lords of Death, faints with terror and wanders in saṃsāra. The deities are as vast as the sky, or as Mount Meru, or at the least as tall as eighteen of one's own bodies stacked up; all that appears dawns as light and bodies, one's own appearance, and to recognise this is perfect buddhahood in a single instant. If one does not, the peaceful ones dawn as the Black Protector and the wrathful ones as Yama, the Lord of Death, King of the Teaching, who comes filling the world, biting his lip, holding his tally-stick, crying 'Strike! Kill!', drinking brains and tearing out hearts. Learning and an aeon of practice are no help without recognition; with it, one key point and one word are enough. The dead person has a body of mind and cannot die; he is the form of emptiness, and emptiness cannot harm emptiness; nothing of all this exists outside his own awareness. The part ends with the call on the yidam: the dead person is to take refuge, remember the Three Jewels and his own yidam, and call on him by name for help.
